eligibility.quote: The `link_t-tool0` transform defining the orientation of the `tool0` frame currently specifies only a rotation over Z of `-pi`, but it uses the value `3.1416` for it ([here](https://github.com/ros-industrial/motoman/blob/e2384f02d926da5b9716fdf915783af31962138c/motoman_sia20d_support/urdf/sia20d_macro.xacro#L188)).

failed_conditions.quote: The difference is enough to cause the `base->tool0` transform to be off by as much as 3 degrees wrt to the values reported by the robot.

loudness.quote: The difference is enough to cause the `base->tool0` transform to be off by as much as 3 degrees wrt to the values reported by the robot.

resolution.quote:
sia20: don't round PI in joint_t-tool0 transform. Fix #106.

Leads to incorrect 'base->tool0' transform orientations.

notes: Sources opened: issue #106 body and comments (gh api) - gavanderhoorn's report (quoted), 'Similar to #102.', 'The SIA10F (and I assume the D) has the same problem', 'SIA10D urdf doesn't have this problem, as it doesn't have a `tool0` link.', closing comment 'Fixed in 9bf25ea.'; fix commit 9bf25ea (gh api): message 'Fix for issue #106: use full-precision PI for tool0 transform (#110)', parent 2d42582c, diffs change sia10f and sia20d macro xacro from '<origin xyz="0 0 0.0" rpy="0 0 -3.1416"/>' to 'rpy="0 0 -3.1415926535"'; sia20d_macro.xacro at e2384f02 via raw.githubusercontent line 188 verified verbatim ('<origin xyz="0 0 0.0" rpy="0 0 -3.1416"/>' on joint link_t-tool0). Eligibility: agree, stop 6. E1: public maintainer issue naming the defect and effect, closed with the fix. E2 step 1: motoman_sia20d_support (provider of the robot_description content) and the node consuming it to compute base->tool0 (taken as robot_state_publisher; the source names no consumer - the spec itself flags this inference and offers MoveIt as the alternative, which would carry the same wrong value across the same parameter). Step 2: a wrong frame-rotation value crossing the robot_description boundary into the consumer's transform computation - the rubric counts a wrong value/frame crossing the boundary as an interface failure even though the resolving edit is inside the provider. Steps 3-5: the fix rewrites an rpy value in the URDF, not a name binding, not build, not firmware. Stop 6, parameter. Failed condition: class frame_mismatch agreed - the defect is the tool0 frame's orientation definition crossing the boundary (a numeric-precision alternative reading as 'other' exists, but frame_mismatch is the closest named class and the spec records the reasoning); element param:/robot_description agreed (the inventory's only element, the carrier of the URDF). Loudness silent_documented/run agreed: the URDF parses, loads and publishes with no diagnostic; the wrong orientation was found only by comparing the computed transform with the robot at run time. Resolution recommended agreed: fix merged and issue closed with 'Fixed in 9bf25ea.', but the source never shows the corrected base->tool0 transform re-compared with the robot, so the resolved composition is not observed. Magnitude caveat (already recorded in the spec's notes, worth keeping visible): 3.1416 - pi is about 7.3e-6 rad (about 0.0004 degrees), which cannot by itself account for the reported 'as much as 3 degrees'; the reporter's figure is recorded verbatim, and the defect (rounded rotation) is real and fixed.
